findings.evidence: "In the canonical operating point — low batch — decode sits in the bandwidth-bound regime. It is like pushing the water of that same 140 GB reservoir through a standard garden hose. On a single device, the full 140 GB must stream within each 25 ms step to produce one token" (printed p. 22); then on printed p. 16: "the canonical 8×H100 host each GPU streams only its 17.5 GB shard — 17.5×10^9 B read against 3.35×10^12 B/s over the 0.025 s step, or ~21% of peak bandwidth".
findings.issue: The §2.2 Mental Model still anchors its decode metaphor on the single-device 140 GB / 25 ms framing, while the chapter's own opening (printed p. 16) insists the 8×H100 host's binding terms are TP collectives, kernel efficiency, sampling, scheduling and the ~9.2K KV read — not the weight read (~21% of peak). The chapter explicitly states the 'bandwidth-bound' verdict from 5.6 TB/s vs 3.35 TB/s is 'the hypothetical whole-model-on-one-GPU case', yet §2.2 re-narrates it as the canonical mental model, and the sentence 'the diameter of the hose (HBM bandwidth) physically cannot move that volume of water in that time frame' reasserts the saturation verdict the opening section disclaims.
findings.fix_instruction: In §2.2's decode paragraph, replace the 140 GB / 25 ms garden-hose sentence with the sharded per-GPU statement (~17.5 GB shard, ~5.2 ms at peak, ~21% of the 25 ms step) and add a one-line pointer that the whole-model-on-one-device 140 GB/5.6 TB/s case is the hypothetical single-device roofline illustration, not the canonical host verdict. Keep the operating-point caveat, but do not let the metaphor contradict the chapter's stated binding terms.

findings.evidence: "weight-only arithmetic intensity ≈ 9,200 FLOP/byte — an upper bound that omits the ~24 GB KV write; adding that write to the denominator lowers the intensity to ≈ 7,850 FLOP/byte"
findings.issue: Check: prefill linear FLOPs = 1.29 PFLOP = 1.29×10^15 FLOP. Weight bytes = 140 GB = 1.4×10^11 B. 1.29×10^15 / 1.4×10^11 = 9,214 FLOP/byte ≈ 9,200. Correct. Adding ~24 GB KV write to denominator: total bytes = 140 + 24 = 164 GB = 1.64×10^11 B. 1.29×10^15 / 1.64×10^11 = 7,866 ≈ 7,850. Close enough (the text says ≈7,850, actual is 7,866 — a 0.2% difference, within the '≈' tolerance). Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "prefill 1.29 PFLOP / (8 × 0.989 PFLOPS) = 0.16 s at peak, ~0.47 s at 35% MFU"
"Decode shard 70B/8 = 8.75B params = 17.5 GB/GPU per step → 17.5 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 5.2 ms at peak"
findings.issue: 70/8 = 8.75B params. 8.75B × 2 bytes = 17.5 GB. Correct. 17.5 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 17.5×10^9 / 3.35×10^12 = 0.005224 s = 5.2 ms. Correct. Then: '5.2 ms ... ~21% of the 25 ms TPOT step'. 5.2/25 = 0.208 ≈ 21%. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

This formula appears at least three times in the provided text (Ch 2 p.17, Ch 4 p.87, and the Reading conventions section p.xviii). All three occurrences are consistent: four terms (retrieval, admission/queue, tokenization/transfer, prefill). The text also consistently states the canonical 1.2 s budget covers only two terms (retrieval + prefill). No inconsistency found across occurrences — verified correct.

findings.evidence: Figure 2.2 caption states: "markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)... both plotted intensities are weight-only: the prefill marker is the ~9.2K FLOP/byte figure before the ~24 GB KV write is counted". However, the text in Section 2.3.1 (Page 53) and Table 2-2 states "Prefill: regime verdict... weight-only arithmetic intensity ~9,200 FLOP/byte". This value (9200) corresponds to 1.29 PFLOP / 140 GB. But the table also lists "Prefill: FLOPs... 1.29 PFLOP" derived from "2 x 70B x 9200 tokens". 2*70e9*9200 = 1.288e15 FLOPs. 1.288e15 / 140e9 bytes = 9200 FLOP/byte. This is correct. The defect is in the text on Page 51: "Decode: required bandwidth... 5.6 TB/s... 140 GB / 0.025 s". 140e9 / 0.025 = 5.6e12 = 5.6 TB/s. This is correct. The defect is actually a missing label or inconsistency in unit definition. On page 51, Table 2-2, row "Decode: required bandwidth..." says "5.6 TB/s". Row "H100 HBM3 peak" says "3.35 TB/s". Row "Decode: required bandwidth per GPU" says "700 GB/s". 140GB/8 GPUs = 17.5GB/GPU. 17.5e9 / 0.025 = 700e9 = 700 GB/s. This is consistent.
findings.issue: I found no P1 arithmetic error in Ch 2 after re-verification. Withdraw F02 to prevent false positive.

findings.evidence: Table 2-2, row "Prefill: single-H100 capacity". Derivation: "1.29 PFLOP / ~1.08 s = 1.19 PFLOPS demand".
findings.issue: Unit inconsistency. The demand is calculated as PFLOP / s = PFLOPS. The text says "1.19 PFLOPS demand". The H100 capacity is "0.989 PFLOPS". The conclusion "demand > peak" is valid. However, the row label "Prefill: single-H100 capacity" is misleading; it describes a *verdict* on feasibility, not the capacity itself. The capacity is 0.989 PFLOPS. The demand is 1.19 PFLOPS.
findings.fix_instruction: Rename the row to "Prefill: single-H100 feasibility check" or similar to distinguish demand vs capacity.
